Prompt_Question: Who is legally considered the frontline field underwriter?
Answer_Target: The insurance producer (agent or broker).
Exam_Trap_Warning: Underwriters in the home office make final decisions, but the producer is the field underwriter.

Prompt_Question: How must an error on a paper insurance application be corrected?
Answer_Target: Line through the error and have the applicant initial it, or complete a brand new application.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Never use whiteout or correction fluid; producers cannot initial for the applicant.

Prompt_Question: Under NYIL § 3105, are applicant statements considered warranties or representations?
Answer_Target: Representations (believed true to the best of knowledge and belief).
Exam_Trap_Warning: Breach of representation only voids coverage if MATERIAL to the risk.

Prompt_Question: When must insurable interest exist in accident and health insurance?
Answer_Target: At the time of application / inception ONLY.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Never at the time of claim or loss (that is the property insurance rule).

Prompt_Question: What information is contained in a Medical Information Bureau (MIB) report?
Answer_Target: Coded medical impairment history reported by member insurers.
Exam_Trap_Warning: No credit reports, no moral character interviews, no physician physical examination records.

Prompt_Question: What does an underwriter do if an application is submitted incomplete?
Answer_Target: Return the application to the producer for completion.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Never accept an incomplete app with answers added later. Issuing without answers waives defenses.

Prompt_Question: When is coverage effective under a Conditional Receipt?
Answer_Target: Date of application or date of required medical exam, whichever is LATER (if insurable as applied).
Exam_Trap_Warning: A medical exam pushes the effective date to the exam date, not the application date.

Prompt_Question: What must be collected upon delivery if the application was NOT prepaid?
Answer_Target: Full initial premium AND a signed Statement of Continued Good Health.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Statement of Good Health is NOT required if application was prepaid with conditional receipt.

Prompt_Question: When does the 10-day (or 30-day) Free Look period begin?
Answer_Target: On the date the policy is physically delivered to the policyowner.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Never starts on the application date, policy date, or issue date.

Prompt_Question: What is the mandatory Free Look period for Long-Term Care, MediGap, and Replacement in NY?
Answer_Target: 30 days with a 100% full refund of all premiums paid.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Standard individual policies have 10-20 days; special consumer policies get 30 days.

Prompt_Question: What is the difference between a Peril and a Hazard?
Answer_Target: Peril is the cause of loss (sickness/injury); Hazard is a condition that increases the chance of loss.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Slippery ice or smoking is a hazard; a broken bone or cancer is a peril.

Prompt_Question: What is the difference between Moral and Morale hazard?
Answer_Target: Moral = dishonesty/fraud; Morale = carelessness/indifference because insured.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Filing a fake claim is moral; leaving doors unlocked is morale.

Prompt_Question: In cost-sharing, what order do Deductible, Coinsurance, and Out-of-Pocket Max apply?
Answer_Target: Deductible first, then Coinsurance split, until Out-of-Pocket Maximum is met.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Always subtract the deductible before calculating the coinsurance split!

Prompt_Question: Under the Coordination of Benefits Birthday Rule, which parent's plan is primary?
Answer_Target: The parent whose birthday (month and day) falls earlier in the calendar year.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Birth year / chronological age is completely irrelevant.

Prompt_Question: What is the legal purpose of the Subrogation provision?
Answer_Target: Allows the insurer to sue the negligent third party to recover claim payments and prevent double recovery.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Prevents the insured from collecting from both insurance and a lawsuit.

Prompt_Question: How are benefits from an employer-paid group disability policy taxed to the employee?
Answer_Target: 100% taxable as ordinary income.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Because employer deducted premiums, employee pays tax on benefits.

Prompt_Question: How are benefits from an individual personally paid disability policy taxed?
Answer_Target: 100% income tax-free.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Because individual paid premiums with post-tax dollars.

Prompt_Question: How are premiums and benefits treated for Business Overhead Expense (BOE)?
Answer_Target: Premiums are tax-deductible; benefits are taxable as income (offset by deductible expenses).
Exam_Trap_Warning: BOE keeps the office open; Key Person disability is NOT deductible.

Prompt_Question: Can comprehensive individual or group major medical policies exclude pre-existing conditions under ACA?
Answer_Target: No. Pre-existing condition exclusions are strictly prohibited.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Pre-existing exclusions remain legal only in limited/excepted policies.

Prompt_Question: What are the three statutory health grace periods under NYIL § 3216?
Answer_Target: 7 days (weekly), 10 days (monthly), 31 days (all other modes).
Exam_Trap_Warning: Do not assume all grace periods are 31 days. Monthly is 10 days!

Prompt_Question: What is the reinstatement waiting period for sickness coverage?
Answer_Target: 10 days (accidental injuries are covered immediately).
Exam_Trap_Warning: Prevents adverse selection; 45 days is automatic approval timeframe.

Prompt_Question: What is the 20-15-90-60-3 claims timeline sequence?
Answer_Target: 20 days Notice of Claim; 15 days Claim Forms; 90 days Proof of Loss; wait 60 days for Legal Action; 3 yrs max suit.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Notice of claim tells them you are hurt; proof of loss provides the bills.

Prompt_Question: Under the Time of Payment of Claims provision, how frequently must periodic disability benefits be paid?
Answer_Target: At least monthly.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Insurer cannot hold disability benefits to pay annually.

Prompt_Question: What happens if an insured changes to a more hazardous job under the Change of Occupation provision?
Answer_Target: The insurer reduces benefits to what the premium would have purchased at the hazardous rate.
Exam_Trap_Warning: In Life insurance, the policy remains as issued. In Disability, benefits are reduced.

Prompt_Question: What does a Noncancelable renewability provision guarantee?
Answer_Target: Insurer cannot cancel AND cannot increase premium rates.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Guaranteed Renewable prevents cancellation but permits class rate increases.

Prompt_Question: What is the waiting period for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)?
Answer_Target: 5 full calendar months (benefits begin in month 6).
Exam_Trap_Warning: Disability must be expected to last at least 12 months or result in death.

Prompt_Question: How many days of inpatient hospital care are covered in a Medicare Part A benefit period?
Answer_Target: 90 days (days 1-60 fully paid; days 61-90 daily copay) + 60 lifetime reserve days.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Benefit period ends when patient has been out of hospital/SNF for 60 consecutive days.

Prompt_Question: Can a producer sell a MediGap policy to an individual enrolled in Medicare Advantage (Part C)?
Answer_Target: No. It is strictly illegal under federal and New York law.
Exam_Trap_Warning: MediGap only supplements Original Medicare (Parts A & B).

Prompt_Question: What is the maximum cash weekly benefit and duration under New York Disability Benefits Law (NY DBL)?
Answer_Target: 50% of Average Weekly Wage up to $170/week maximum, for up to 26 weeks.
Exam_Trap_Warning: NY DBL covers off-the-job sickness only and provides ZERO medical care.

Prompt_Question: What does the New York State Partnership for Long-Term Care provide?
Answer_Target: Total Asset Protection from New York Medicaid spend-down after exhausting policy benefits.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Insured keeps all personal assets while Medicaid covers nursing care.

Prompt_Question: What are the two core features of an HMO?
Answer_Target: Closed provider network and Primary Care Physician (PCP) gatekeeper for specialist visits.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Zero out-of-network coverage except for true emergencies.

Prompt_Question: How does an Exclusive Provider Organization (EPO) differ from an HMO?
Answer_Target: EPO requires in-network care like an HMO, but does NOT require a PCP gatekeeper referral.
Exam_Trap_Warning: EPO members have direct access to in-network specialists.

Prompt_Question: What is the difference between Own Occupation and Any Occupation disability?
Answer_Target: Own Occ = unable to do own specific job; Any Occ = unable to do any job suited by education/training.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Own Occ is easier to claim and costs higher premium.

Prompt_Question: What triggers benefits under a Hospital Indemnity (Confinement) policy?
Answer_Target: Hospital confinement pays a flat daily cash dollar benefit regardless of actual medical bills.
Exam_Trap_Warning: Does not pay medical expenses or doctor bills; pays cash to the insured.

Prompt_Question: What is the core peril covered by Long-Term Care insurance, and what is Respite Care?
Answer_Target: Peril is Aging / loss of ADLs; Respite care provides temporary relief to primary family caregivers.
Exam_Trap_Warning: LTC covers aging, not acute medical illness.
